free_tier.stated: Per-item size is set by the game developer, not by Valve, and some games are explicitly unlimited — Arma 3: 'Arma 3 Workshop now support items of unlimited size.' Others are tiny: House Flipper raised its cap from 12 MB to 20 MB in a patch. So the quota is per-app, and the number of published items per account is not documented as capped.

egress.terms: Free and CDN-served by Valve's content network — same infrastructure as game downloads, genuinely unmetered.

tooling: `ISteamUGC` (CreateItem + SetItemContent + SubmitItemUpdate) via the Steamworks SDK, so uploads need a Steam client with the game installed. Downloads are scriptable anonymously: `steamcmd +login anonymous +workshop_download_item <appid> <publishedfileid>`. Third-party downloaders (polocaz/ws-downloader, workshopfetch.com) exist for the read path.
chaining: One Steam account x every Workshop-enabled game it owns x unlimited items per game. This is the multiplier: 'unlimited items per published file ID' inside an app whose developer set no cap.

limits.value: review images go through a separate Steam Cloud quota

limits_note: Requires ownership of the game and a Steam client to upload — there is no headless upload path, which is the practical blocker. Per-item caps range from 20 MB to unlimited depending on app; preview images go through a separate Steam Cloud quota.
